summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, and peripheral artery disease was admitted for evaluation of shaking chills following a punch biopsy of a chronic left lower leg ulcer. The biopsy confirmed calciphylaxis, explaining his symptoms. Blood and urine cultures were negative, and antibiotics were discontinued after four days. He underwent successful placement of a port for administration of intravenous sodium thiosulfate, which was initiated during the admission. Cinacalcet was started and vitamin D stopped to manage calcium metabolism. His acute kidney injury resolved with hydration, and his blood pressure was controlled on home medications. He was discharged home with plans for outpatient sodium thiosulfate infusions, wound care, and follow-up with dermatology and transplant nephrology.
